# Fairpractice Therapy Billing (`fairpractice-therapy-billing`)

Checks outpatient therapy billing (PT, OT, speech): visits with no plan of care, certifications unsigned, timed units over the 8-minute rule, missing CQ/CO assistant modifiers and GP/GO/GN discipline modifiers, lines past the yearly KX threshold without KX, and recertifications coming due. Patient names are masked before results reach the model.

**Fairpractice Therapy Billing never submits or changes claims. Fairpractice Therapy Billing never adds KX or any modifier to a claim; a person decides.**

Fairpractice ver 1 · Specialty billing · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · patient and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`fairpractice-core`](../fairpractice-core)

```bash
npx -y fairpractice-therapy-billing demo
npx -y fairpractice-therapy-billing mcp --root ./practice-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional data only: a made-up outpatient therapy clinic, made-up patients and staff. Any likeness to real people is chance.

- [`visits-2026.csv`](fixtures/visits-2026.csv) and [`plans-of-care.csv`](fixtures/plans-of-care.csv). Planted:
  - P1: PT spending passes the KX threshold on November 3 with no KX, and that day bills 4 timed units for 40 timed minutes (the 8-minute rule allows 3).
  - P2: an OT assistant (COTA) bills 97530 with GP and without CO; the OT plan of care from October 1 is still unsigned.
  - P3: the speech plan of care ends November 29 and the patient was seen November 6, so the recertification is due.
  - P4: PT on November 10 falls after the plan of care ended November 5. The PTA line carries CQ, so it is not flagged for the modifier.
- [`settings.json`](fixtures/settings.json): KX threshold 2410 (set your year's figure), Medicare only, 30 days to sign, warn 21 days ahead. [`settings-typo.json`](fixtures/settings-typo.json) misspells a setting and is refused.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `therapy_check` | List visits with no plan of care, unsigned certifications, 8-minute rule overages, modifier problems, KX gaps and recertifications due. | runs |
| `therapy_write_report` | Write therapy.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and therapy.html into out_dir (default fairpractice-out/therapy). | runs |
| `therapy_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `therapy_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `therapy_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `therapy_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `claim_submit` | Fairpractice Therapy Billing never submits or changes claims. | refused |
| `modifier_apply` | Fairpractice Therapy Billing never adds KX or any modifier to a claim; a person decides. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `therapy_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `visits` (required) | Therapy charge lines under --root: patient, date, code, modifiers, units, minutes, provider and role, payer, allowed amount |
| `plans` (required) | Plans of care: patient, discipline (PT, OT, SLP), certification start and end, date signed |
| `settings` | Optional settings JSON: kx_threshold, kx_payers, timed_codes, rates, sign_days, warn_days |
| `as_of` | Date to measure deadlines and ages from (YYYY-MM-DD); default today |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold patient or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx fairpractice-therapy-billing inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Visits (`visits`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `patient_id` | text (masked) | Patient ID, Patient #, Patient Number, MRN, Medical Record Number, Chart #, Chart Number, Account # |
| `patient_name` | text (masked) | Patient, Patient Name, Name, Client, Client Name, Member, Member Name, Beneficiary |
| `date` (required) | date | Date of Service, DOS, Service Date, Visit Date, Date, From DOS, Session Date, Appointment Date |
| `cpt` (required) | text | CPT, Code, Procedure, Procedure Code, CPT/HCPCS, HCPCS, Service Code, Proc Code |
| `modifiers` | text | Modifiers, Modifier, Mod, Mods, Modifier 1, Mod 1 |
| `units` | number | Units, Unit, Qty, Quantity, Days/Units, Service Units |
| `minutes` | number | Minutes, Min, Mins, Duration, Duration (min), Time (min), Total Minutes, Treatment Minutes |
| `provider` | text (masked) | Provider, Rendering Provider, Rendering, Clinician, Therapist, Physician, Doctor, Practitioner |
| `provider_role` | text | Provider Role, Role, Credential, Discipline, Provider Type, Therapist Type |
| `payer` | text | Payer, Payer Name, Primary Payer, Insurance, Insurance Name, Plan, Plan Name, Payor |
| `allowed` | amount | Allowed, Allowed Amount, Expected, Expected Payment, Fee Schedule, Contract Amount |

### Plans of care (`plans`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `patient_id` (required) | text (masked) | Patient ID, Patient #, Patient Number, MRN, Medical Record Number, Chart #, Chart Number, Account # |
| `patient_name` | text (masked) | Patient, Patient Name, Name, Client, Client Name, Member, Member Name, Beneficiary |
| `discipline` | text | Discipline, Therapy, Therapy Type, Service, Service Line |
| `start` (required) | date | Start, Start Date, Cert Start, Certification Start, From, POC Start, Plan Start |
| `end` | date | End, End Date, Cert End, Certification End, Through, Thru, POC End, Plan End |
| `signed` | date | Signed, Signed Date, Physician Signed, Signature Date, Certified On, Date Signed |

## Settings file (`therapy_settings`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `kx_threshold` | Yearly KX threshold amount for your year (CMS publishes it each year; check the current figure); default 2410 |
| `kx_payers` | Words in payer names the KX threshold applies to; default ["medicare"] |
| `timed_codes` | Timed codes counted under the 8-minute rule |
| `rates` | Expected payment per unit by code, used when the file has no allowed amount |
| `sign_days` | Days after the plan start to have the certification signed; default 30 |
| `warn_days` | Days ahead to warn about plans of care ending; default 21 |

## Memory

`therapy_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `therapy_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `fairpractice-core` and `fairclaim-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fairpractice-therapy-billing": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "fairpractice-therapy-billing",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/practice-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add fairpractice-therapy-billing -- npx -y fairpractice-therapy-billing mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
fairpractice-therapy-billing tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
fairpractice-therapy-billing sources               # the columns each input is read from
fairpractice-therapy-billing inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
fairpractice-therapy-billing call therapy_check '{"visits":"<visits>","plans":"<plans>"}'
fairpractice-therapy-billing eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
fairpractice-therapy-billing demo
```

## Patient and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: patient and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to an EHR, practice-management system, payer portal, clearinghouse, state system, HR or payroll system, or bank.
- Payer, Medicare, Medicaid, state and federal rules are summarised from public material as of 2026, and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, compliance or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, billing, coding, tax, clinical or HIPAA advice. It does not diagnose or recommend care. A person decides what to bill, pay, report, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
